content:
Apple has filed for an injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple says it will suffer "irreparable harm" from the alleged theft of its trade secrets if a preliminary injunction is not granted.

In its filing, Apple explains that, after filing its initial lawsuit last month, the company reached out to OpenAI and stated its "intention to seek preliminary injunctive relief." However, Apple says OpenAI could avoid this step if it agreed to five conditions:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other repositories
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any of Apple's confidential information

According to Apple, OpenAI agreed to the first three conditions, but the two sides could not reach agreement on the final two.

As a result, Apple is asking the court to issue a preliminary injunction that would immediately bar OpenAI from using or accessing any of Apple's trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and recover any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple says:

Apple has also filed a separate motion asking the court to expedite discovery, including early document production and depositions of key OpenAI employees and management outside of court.

Alongside these filings, OpenAI has issued its most extensive public response to the Apple lawsuit to date. In a blog post published late at night, OpenAI said the "careless, aggressive, and inexplicably targeted lawsuit" is not befitting of Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

The injunction hearing is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full filing is available below.
